question: In the Soxhlet extraction of macaw palm almond oil, how much hexane and how much almond were used per unit, and for how long at what temperature?
expect: 125 mL hexane for about 17 g almond (about 1:7.3 m/v), about 5 h at about 70 C (sec. on oil extraction)
trap: the 60 C oven used to evaporate hexane
rendered:
Thermophysical and Chemical Evaluation of Macaw Palm Almond Oil as a Biobased Heat-Transfer Fluid Candidate for Medium-Temperature Solar Thermal Applications

2.2. Oil Preparation and Extraction

Oil extraction was performed using the Soxhlet method, selected due to its high extraction efficiency for lipid recovery from oleaginous matrices. Three extraction cartridges were prepared using filter paper and filled with previously weighed crushed almond samples.

The extraction system consisted of three 1 L round-bottom flasks connected to Soxhlet extractors and condensers. In each extraction unit, 125 mL of hexane was used as the solvent for approximately 17 g of macauba palm almond, resulting in a solvent-to-sample ratio of approximately 1:7.3 (m/v). The extraction process was conducted for approximately 5 h at about 70 °C using heating mantles.

The answer is: 125 mL of hexane and approximately 17 g of macauba palm almond, at a solvent-to-sample ratio of approximately 1:7.3 (m/v), for approximately 5 h at about 70 °C.
